annotationRationale: A shifted product restricts the integer gcd-lcm pairs to finitely many possibilities. Divisibility and prime-exponent structure then determine every ordered pair a,b.
sourceMethod: Followed the official gcd-lcm substitution and shifted factorization. Explicitly excluded negative factor pairs to complete the enumeration.

review.mathCheck: The equation becomes \((x-12)(y-20)=177\). Negative factors are correctly excluded. Of the four positive-factor possibilities, only \((x,y)=(189,21)\) satisfies \(y\mid x\). The prime-exponent conditions force \((a,b)=(21,189)\) or its reverse. Both satisfy the equation, giving 2, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA solution 23, pages 10–11: shifted-product factorization, gcd–lcm divisibility, then prime-exponent reconstruction. The candidate also justifies the exclusion of negative factors omitted in the source.
